chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
I said: A woman sees purity at noon, then occupies herself with her affair until the time of ʿaṣr enters. He said, “She prays ʿaṣr alone; but if she neglects it, then two prayers are upon her.”

key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: ritual purity after the end of menstruation
key_terms.صَلَاتَانِ: two prayers, meaning both ẓuhr and ʿaṣr
key_terms.ضَيَّعَتْ: she neglected or let it lapse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman becomes pure from menstruation at ẓuhr but delays until ʿaṣr time begins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who becomes pure from menstruation around the time of ẓuhr but delays until the time of ʿaṣr begins. It indicates that if she reaches the time of ʿaṣr without having performed ẓuhr, she performs ʿaṣr alone, and if she further neglects the matter, liability for both prayers applies.
